subject: math
title: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding Multi-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Place Value and Rounding Worksheets: Expanded Form, Comparing and Rounding to Any Place
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right. Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols. Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 place value worksheets: value of a digit up to 1,000,000, ten times the place to the right, standard, word and expanded form, comparing with >, = and <, and rounding to any place with number lines. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. Compare from the left; round by looking one place to the right.
key_sub: The 7 in 70,000 is worth 10 times the 7 in 7,000. Write a 0 in every empty place, count digits before comparing, and remember that a 5 rounds up.
body_html:
Each place is 10 times the place to its right

A digit's value depends on its place. Move one place to the left, and the value becomes 10 times as much. 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand, and so on.

Ten times

In 44,000, how does the first 4 compare to the second 4?

The first 4 is in the ten thousands place: 40,000. The second 4 is in the thousands place: 4,000. 40,000 = 10 × 4,000.

Answer: The first 4 is worth 10 times as much

Three ways to write a number

Form305,040
Standard form305,040
Word formthree hundred five thousand, forty
Expanded form300,000 + 5,000 + 40

In word form, read the part before the comma, say “thousand”, then read the last 3 digits. Never say “and” in a whole number. In standard form, write a 0 in every empty place.

Compare from the left

First count the digits: more digits means a greater number. If they have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

45,309 ☐ 45,390

Ten thousands: 4 = 4. Thousands: 5 = 5. Hundreds: 3 = 3. Tens: 0 < 9.

Answer: 45,309 < 45,390

Round to any place

  1. Find the digit in the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit one place to its right.
  3. 5 or more: add 1 to the rounding digit. 4 or less: keep it.
  4. Change every digit to the right of the rounding place to 0. Digits on the left stay the same, unless a 9 regroups.
Round 284,516 to the nearestLook atAnswer
ten6 ones284,520
hundred1 ten284,500
thousand5 hundreds285,000
ten thousand4 thousands280,000
hundred thousand8 ten thousands300,000
Watch the 9s

Round 499,999 to the nearest thousand.

The thousands digit is 9. The digit to its right is 9, so round up. 499,000 + 1,000 = 500,000.

Answer: 500,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 472,615 is 7)Multiply by the place: 7 × 10,000 = 70,000
Leaving out zeros (forty thousand six = 4,006)Write 3 digits after the comma: 40,006
Comparing the first digits only (98,765 > 102,345)Count the digits first: 6 digits beat 5 digits
Rounding 96,500 down to 96,000A 5 rounds up: 97,000
Rounding to the wrong place (64,350 to the nearest ten thousand = 64,000)Find the ten thousands digit first: 60,000

faq.q: What place value should a 4th grader know?
faq.a: Grade 4 students work with whole numbers up to 1,000,000. They read and write them in standard, word and expanded form, and know that each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

faq.q: What is expanded form in 4th grade math?
faq.a: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the values of its digits. For example, 52,078 = 50,000 + 2,000 + 70 + 8.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest ten thousand?
faq.a: Find the ten thousands digit, then look at the thousands digit to its right. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. 64,350 rounds to 60,000.

faq.q: How do you compare two large numbers?
faq.a: Count the digits first; the number with more digits is greater. If they have the same number of digits, compare from the left until two digits are different.

sets.title: Each place is 10 times the place to its right

items.q: What is 10 × 6,000?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 6 thousands become 6 ten thousands. 6,000 × 10 = 60,000.

items.q: What is 10 × 400?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 4 hundreds become 4 thousands. 400 × 10 = 4,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 9 ten thousands become 9 hundred thousands. 90,000 × 10 = 900,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 1 hundred thousand becomes 1 million. 100,000 × 10 = 1,000,000.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 7 ten thousands become 7 thousands. 70,000 ÷ 10 = 7,000.

items.q: What is 5,000 ÷ 10?
items.e: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 5 thousands become 5 hundreds. 5,000 ÷ 10 = 500.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 2 hundred thousands become 2 ten thousands. 200,000 ÷ 10 = 20,000.

items.q: How many tens are in 900?

items.q: Three baseball games had these crowds: 35,841 fans, 35,418 fans and 31,548 fans. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 31,548 < 35,418, because in the thousands place 1 < 5. 35,418 < 35,841, because in the hundreds place 4 < 8. So the order is 31,548; 35,418; 35,841.

items.q: Three towns have these populations: 46,587 people, 48,657 people and 45,687 people. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 45,687 < 46,587, because in the thousands place 5 < 6. 46,587 < 48,657, because in the thousands place 6 < 8. So the order is 45,687; 46,587; 48,657.

items.q: Three trucks have driven 415,237 miles, 417,235 miles and 415,732 miles. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 415,237 < 415,732, because in the hundreds place 2 < 7. 415,732 < 417,235, because in the thousands place 5 < 7. So the order is 415,237; 415,732; 417,235.

items.q: Last month, three websites had 681,325 visits, 685,123 visits and 682,135 visits. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 681,325 < 682,135, because in the thousands place 1 < 2. 682,135 < 685,123, because in the thousands place 2 < 5. So the order is 681,325; 682,135; 685,123.

sets.title: Round to any place and word problems

items.q: Round 3,482 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 3,482 is between 3,400 and 3,500. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 8, so round up. Answer: 3,500.

items.q: Round 96,500 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 96,500 is exactly halfway between 96,000 and 97,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 97,000.

items.q: Round 64,350 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest ten thousand: 64,350 is between 60,000 and 70,000. The digit to the right of the ten thousands place is 4, so round down. Answer: 60,000.

items.q: Round 28,716 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 28,716 is between 28,000 and 29,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 7, so round up. Answer: 29,000.

items.q: Round 372,904 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred thousand: 372,904 is between 300,000 and 400,000. The digit to the right of the hundred thousands place is 7, so round up. Answer: 400,000.

items.q: Round 845,230 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest ten thousand: 845,230 is between 840,000 and 850,000. The digit to the right of the ten thousands place is 5, so round up. Answer: 850,000.

items.q: Round 38,465 to the nearest ten.
items.e: Round to the nearest ten: 38,465 is exactly halfway between 38,460 and 38,470. The digit to the right of the tens place is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 38,470.

items.q: Round 499,999 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 499,999 is between 499,000 and 500,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 9, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so adding 1 thousand regroups: 499,000 + 1,000 = 500,000. Answer: 500,000.

items.q: Round 79,581 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 79,581 is between 79,500 and 79,600. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 8, so round up. Answer: 79,600.

items.q: Round 209,617 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest ten thousand: 209,617 is between 200,000 and 210,000. The digit to the right of the ten thousands place is 9, so round up. Answer: 210,000.

items.q: Round 649,999 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred thousand: 649,999 is between 600,000 and 700,000. The digit to the right of the hundred thousands place is 4, so round down. Answer: 600,000.

items.q: Round 51,962 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 51,962 is between 51,000 and 52,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 9, so round up. Answer: 52,000.

items.q: A park had 72,480 visitors this year. A sign says “about 72,000 visitors.” To which place was the number rounded?
items.e: 72,480 to the nearest thousand: the hundreds digit is 4, so round down to 72,000. To the nearest hundred it would be 72,500, and to the nearest ten thousand it would be 70,000.

items.q: A school district has 24,951 students. What is that number rounded to the nearest hundred?
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 24,951 is between 24,900 and 25,000. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 5, so round up. The hundreds digit is 9, so adding 1 hundred regroups: 24,900 + 100 = 25,000. Answer: 25,000.

items.q: What is the greatest whole number that rounds to 50,000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: Numbers from 49,500 to 50,499 round to 50,000. 50,500 has a 5 in the hundreds place, so it rounds up to 51,000.

items.q: A video has 349,612 views. Rounded to the nearest hundred thousand, about how many views is that?
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred thousand: 349,612 is between 300,000 and 400,000. The digit to the right of the hundred thousands place is 4, so round down. Answer: 300,000.

items.q: At a baseball game, 41,736 fans were in the stadium. A news report rounds this to the nearest thousand. What number does the report give?
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 41,736 is between 41,000 and 42,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 7, so round up. Answer: 42,000.

items.q: Leo's family drove 1,486 miles on a road trip. What is that distance rounded to the nearest hundred?
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 1,486 is between 1,400 and 1,500. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 8, so round up. Answer: 1,500.

items.q: A city has 284,516 people. What is its population rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: Round to the nearest ten thousand: 284,516 is between 280,000 and 290,000. The digit to the right of the ten thousands place is 4, so round down. Answer: 280,000.

items.q: A concert sold about 30,000 tickets, rounded to the nearest ten thousand. Which could be the exact number of tickets sold?
items.e: Numbers from 25,000 to 34,999 round to 30,000. 25,104 is in that range. 35,200 and 38,000 round up to 40,000, and 24,870 rounds down to 20,000.
